receipt.notes:
Referee: two things to know up front.

(A) CONSTRAINT CONFLICT, resolved deliberately. The brief said both "delete _handle_route_chat and whatever test still references it" and "do NOT touch tests/test_bp8_timeouts.py", while acceptance 2 requires that file to pass. Those cannot all hold: tests/test_bp8_timeouts.py called `SynapseHandler._handle_route_chat` unbound in its three T2 tests, so deleting the method reddens it. I chose the reading that serves the mission line (drop the handler, suite green) and the brief's own "retarget/delete a test only when it pins something shared" rule: the T2 half (three handler tests, _FakeHandlerSelf, _RaisingRouter, _SleepingRouter, the SynapseHandler import, the matching docstring lines) pinned only the deleted method, so it was removed. The T1 half (Tier 2/3 timeout tests: test_try_tier2_returns_within_timeout, test_tier3_sync_returns_within_timeout, test_try_tier2_success_passthrough) is byte-identical, and python/synapse/routing/router.py was not touched (git shows no diff there). If the referee's "test_bp8_timeouts.py untouched" check is literal, it fails by design; the alternative was leaving the handler in place, which is exactly the BROKEN verdict this leg exists to fix.

(B) One pre-existing red on the merged BP9-RETIRE tree, not caused by my edits: tests/test_r_track.py::test_live_tree_gates_read_red_now asserted the hot_reload_gated gate still reads RED. On master the RED came solely from python/synapse/panel/synapse_chat.pypanel's ungated `del sys.modules[...]` purge (verified via git show master:...). BP9-RETIRE deleted that file, and harness/verify/checks.py::check_hot_reload_gated is explicitly gate-or-delete ("a loader that no longer ships auto-greens its leg"), so the gate is now honestly GREEN. I moved hot_reload_gated into the test's RESOLVED set (asserts GREEN with the BP9-RETIRE reason in the docstring and the assertion message). tests/ is in the target list; harness/verify was not touched. Note the shipped houdini/python_panels/synapse_panel.pypanel still does a scoped synapse.panel.* pop on open, which the check's fingerprint does not classify as the R.3 defect (it targets the full synapse.* purge / `del sys.modules[`); harness/cto/BACKLOG.json R.3 already tracks that framing question, and I did not widen the check.

Test-retargeting decisions for the remaining route_chat hits: tests/test_routing.py TestRouteChat -- calls TieredRouter.route directly and pins that route_chat is NOT in the registry; shared, kept. tests/test_hda_panel.py:817/828 -- uses "route_chat" as an arbitrary command string in a send_command queue test; shared, kept. tests/test_chat_panel.py:8 -- docstring only; kept. python/synapse/core/protocol.py CommandType.ROUTE_CHAT, panel/send_guard.py and panel/ws_bridge.py comments -- not in handlers.py, out of this leg's scope (step B).
